title_reveal.description: USE WHEN: bullet wants ONE hero word (or very short phrase) to land with weight, optional subtitle below. DON'T USE WHEN: hero element is a number/percentage (use number_punch); line is a question (use provocation).

title_card.description: USE WHEN: bullet wants a single line of typed text as a label, beat-card, or callout, optional accent color token. DON'T USE WHEN: line is a question (use provocation), a quote (use pull_quote), or a hero word (use title_reveal). Color value, when provided, must be a token name from the project's config.yaml design block.

number_punch.description: USE WHEN: bullet wants a SEQUENCE of single-line elements (numbers, percentages, short words/phrases) to slot-machine in one at a time, big and centered, hard spring + shake. DON'T USE WHEN: elements are paired number+label structure (use stats_grid) or side-by-side comparison (use split_screen).

provocation.description: USE WHEN: bullet poses a question or rhetorical statement, typewriter delivery with blinking cursor. DON'T USE WHEN: line is a statement of fact (use title_card) or a quote (use pull_quote).

bullet_list.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows a list of N items (any N) that should spring in with stagger, optional title above. DON'T USE WHEN: items are checkable/completable (use checklist) or items are number+label pairs (use stats_grid).

formula.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows a short equation/relationship as N tokens that should appear word-by-word with optional per-token colors. Intent examples: X = Y + Z, A vs B, FAST != SLOW. DON'T USE WHEN: line is prose (use title_card) or arithmetic with computed values (no primitive today).

checklist.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows N items that get bouncy check stamps as they appear — capabilities, requirements, completed work. DON'T USE WHEN: items are not binary done/not-done (use bullet_list).

stats_grid.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows N number+label pairs side-by-side as a scoreboard. DON'T USE WHEN: there is only one big number (use number_punch).

split_screen.description: USE WHEN: bullet wants a left/right vertical split with a label per side, optionally a value per side; strong VS energy. DON'T USE WHEN: comparison is racing/animated (use benchmark_race) or three+ way (split into multiple bullets or use stats_grid).

model_orb_with_components.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows a central glowing node with N labeled tools/components arranged around it; radial architecture diagram. Colors are taken from config.yaml design tokens — don't pick them. DON'T USE WHEN: components have specific input/output relationships flowing through the center (use guides_sensors_split).

caption_card.description: USE WHEN: bullet wants a lower-third caption — definition, aside label, secondary context that supports a hero element above. DON'T USE WHEN: the caption IS the hero element (use title_card).

code_flood_terminal.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows a terminal flooding with code at high speed, file paths flickering at top, optional PR counter ticking. DON'T USE WHEN: terminal shows one quiet command (use title_card).

tetris_stack.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows N building-block layers stacking up to construct a concept; each block has a label. Colors are taken from config.yaml design tokens — don't pick them. DON'T USE WHEN: stack order doesn't matter (use bullet_list or checklist).

benchmark_race.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows two models/options racing on a named benchmark with a leaderboard ticking live. DON'T USE WHEN: comparison is static numbers (use stats_grid) or generic split (use split_screen).

closed_loop_circuit.description: USE WHEN: bullet describes a feedback/iteration loop with N stages connecting back to the start (cycle continues). Per-stage colors come from the bullet body if specified, else config.yaml design tokens. DON'T USE WHEN: flow is a linear pipeline (no primitive today).

timeline_playhead.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows progress over time with a playhead sweeping left-to-right, optional counters and milestone events. DON'T USE WHEN: time progression is between discrete versions/releases (use evolution_timeline).

evolution_timeline.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows a generational/version progression with N nodes (year + label); mark current node, optionally mark future node as dotted. DON'T USE WHEN: time is continuous with counters/playhead (use timeline_playhead).

productivity_bars.description: USE WHEN: bullet compares two teams/approaches with one outpacing the other (human-vs-AI, before-vs-after). DON'T USE WHEN: comparison is benchmark scores (use benchmark_race) or stat values (use stats_grid).

mini_ui_grid.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows multiple product UIs / use-case examples in an NxM grid that animate in sequence. Grid shape (rows, columns) is determined by the bullet body, not by this primitive. DON'T USE WHEN: only one UI is shown (use image_asset if a screenshot is on disk).

guides_sensors_split.description: USE WHEN: bullet describes a closed input/output loop with N inputs (guides) on the left feeding into a central node and N outputs (sensors) on the right whose results feed back. DON'T USE WHEN: it's a generic comparison (use split_screen) or a one-way pipeline (no primitive today).

pull_quote.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows a verbatim quotation with attribution. DON'T USE WHEN: text is the author's own statement, not attributed to someone (use title_card).

logo_swarm.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows a list of product/brand names that pop in around a central caption (ecosystem diagram). DON'T USE WHEN: logos are real image assets on disk (use image_asset per logo).

callback_card.description: USE WHEN: bullet wants a small reminder of prior facts/numbers from earlier in the video; smaller scale, often docked to a corner; optional tagline. DON'T USE WHEN: items are new content for this scene (use bullet_list).

silhouette_team.description: USE WHEN: bullet shows N people at desks with floating orbs doing the typing — collaboration / scale of adoption. Orb color comes from config.yaml design tokens, not this primitive. DON'T USE WHEN: people are individual characters (no primitive today).

image_asset.description: USE WHEN: bullet references an image file (logo, screenshot, photo, diagram, SVG) that lives in projects/<name>/public/<filename>. The bullet body either names the file (e.g. '[asset: filename.png]') or describes a real-world image asset that the author has put on disk. The src prop is the filename verbatim. DON'T USE WHEN: the file is not on disk yet (ask the user OR drop the bullet).
